findings.title: NULL-category rows collapse into one partition
findings.problem: The window partitions by (project_name, budget_category) and budget_category is nullable. Any project_budget rows with a NULL category (legacy rows written before the column was populated) share one partition, so only one survives, and _select_category_rows looks it up with assigned_by_category.get(None), which always routes it to the unassigned branch. The current collector always sets the category, so only pre-existing data can trigger this.
findings.impact: If a NULL-category row's budget still has an open period and spend > 0, it is added to Budget Period Spend as an unassigned row on top of the same category's categorised row, overstating spend; the frontend drops it (no category) so the extra amount is invisible in the cards. Reachability unconfirmed: whether NULL-category project_budget rows with open periods exist in production data was not established.
findings.recommendation: Exclude rows with budget_category IS NULL from get_latest_project_budget_rows_by_category (or skip them in _select_category_rows), and cover it with a test.

findings.title: Latest-row tie-break is nondeterministic
findings.problem: Rows are ranked by spend_date DESC, created_at DESC. created_at is server_default NOW(), which is fixed per transaction, and the collector inserts every snapshot of a run with the same spend_date in one session. Two project_budget rows for the same project and category in one run (e.g. a removed budget's key still reporting alongside the new one) tie on both columns, so the kept row is arbitrary, contradicting the docstring's 'the one inserted last wins'.
findings.impact: The selected row can flip between requests, so the category's reported spend and its assigned/unassigned attribution become unstable. Reachability unconfirmed: whether the LiteLLM project snapshot can report two budgets of one category in one run was not established.
findings.recommendation: Add a deterministic final sort key (e.g. ProjectSpendTracking.id or budget_id DESC, or a real insertion sequence) and correct the docstring to match the actual rule.

findings.title: Repository test misses ordering and rank filter
findings.problem: TestLatestProjectBudgetRowsByCategory.test_partitions_by_category_not_budget_id only asserts the PARTITION BY clause, the 'project_budget' literal and the project name in compiled SQL; it never checks the spend_date/created_at DESC ordering or the row_rank = 1 filter that decide which row is 'latest'. Every router test patches this method with hand-built rows, and no DB-backed test exists.
findings.impact: Consumers _attach_project_spending_summaries and _attach_project_detail_spending feed its rows into the project list and detail spend totals; flipping a sort direction, dropping the tie-break or removing the rank filter would return old or all historical rows as current spend with no failing test.
findings.recommendation: Assert 'ORDER BY project_spend_tracking.spend_date DESC, project_spend_tracking.created_at DESC' (plus any added tie-break) and 'row_rank = 1' in the compiled SQL, or add a DB-backed test seeding multiple rows per category and asserting only the newest is returned.
